# GLRMask

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-guide.py from docs/content. Do not edit this output. -->

GLRMask is a grammar-constrained decoding library for high-throughput LLM serving. It is optimized for fast mask computation with extremely low tail latency, even for complex grammars.

GLRMask supports general context-free grammars, including ambiguous ones. It accepts JSON Schema, Lark, and GLRMask's native format: GLRM.

[Website](https://glrmask.com) · [GitHub](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask) · [Paper](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23273556)

## Installation

```bash
cargo add glrmask
```

GLRMask needs Rust 1.89 or later. A minor release may raise the minimum Rust version; a patch release won't.

## Usage

GLRMask has four core types:

- `Grammar`: a grammar, written as source text or built from an expression.
- `Module`: a grammar plus its extern bindings and any precompiled work. Can be saved and loaded.
- `Constraint`: a grammar compiled for a vocabulary, ready to use.
- `ConstraintState`: the state of one generated sequence.

## Quickstart

```rust
use glrmask::{Grammar, Vocab};

fn main() -> glrmask::Result<()> {
    let vocab = Vocab::new(vec![
        (0, b"hello".to_vec()), (1, b" ".to_vec()), (2, b"world".to_vec()),
    ]);
    let grammar = Grammar::from_ebnf(r#"start ::= "hello" " " "world""#)?;
    let constraint = grammar.compile(&vocab)?;
    let mut state = constraint.start();
    for token_id in 0..3 {
        assert_eq!(state.mask()[0], 1 << token_id);
        assert!(state.commit_token(token_id));
    }
    assert!(state.is_accepting());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Learn more

[Full guide](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/GUIDE.md) · [API reference](https://docs.rs/glrmask/latest/glrmask/) · [Benchmarks](https://glrmask.com/#benchmarks)

Native bindings are available for C++ and JavaScript/TypeScript on Node.js. The [C++ guide and C API](https://glrmask.com/api/cpp/) and [JavaScript and TypeScript guide](https://glrmask.com/api/javascript/) cover source builds, platform artifacts, ownership, composition, and the complete supported API. The Node.js addon runs the Rust engine directly; browser WebAssembly is a separate target.
